alerts.title: Successful login after repeated failures
alerts.summary: 'deploy' logged in from 203.0.113.77 after 3 failed attempts in the preceding 15 minutes
evidence: Mar 14 03:16:00 web01 sshd[2450]: Failed password for deploy from 203.0.113.77 port 40100 ssh2
Mar 14 03:16:12 web01 sshd[2450]: Failed password for deploy from 203.0.113.77 port 40105 ssh2
Mar 14 03:16:18 web01 sshd[2450]: Failed password for deploy from 203.0.113.77 port 40111 ssh2
Mar 14 03:16:20 web01 sshd[2455]: Accepted password for deploy from 203.0.113.77 port 40122 ssh2
alerts.recommendation: Treat the account as compromised: force a password reset, revoke sessions and keys, review what the account touched, and check for persistence.

alerts.title: SSH brute-force attempts
alerts.summary: 7 failed SSH logins from 203.0.113.5 within 5 minutes, against 3 username(s)
evidence: Mar 14 03:10:02 web01 sshd[2411]: Failed password for root from 203.0.113.5 port 51422 ssh2
Mar 14 03:10:16 web01 sshd[2411]: Failed password for root from 203.0.113.5 port 51426 ssh2
Mar 14 03:10:31 web01 sshd[2412]: Failed password for admin from 203.0.113.5 port 51431 ssh2
Mar 14 03:11:20 web01 sshd[2414]: Failed password for invalid user oracle from 203.0.113.5 port 51461 ssh2
alerts.recommendation: Block the source, disable password authentication for external SSH, require keys, and consider fail2ban or a bastion host.

alerts.title: Password spraying
alerts.summary: 6 distinct usernames tried from 198.51.100.9 within 15 minutes

entities.users: awilson, jsmith, kgarcia, lbrown, mchen, tpatel

evidence: Mar 14 03:11:40 web01 sshd[2421]: Invalid user jsmith from 198.51.100.9
Mar 14 03:13:05 web01 sshd[2422]: Invalid user awilson from 198.51.100.9
Mar 14 03:14:20 web01 sshd[2423]: Invalid user mchen from 198.51.100.9
Mar 14 03:19:45 web01 sshd[2426]: Invalid user lbrown from 198.51.100.9
alerts.recommendation: Spraying targets many accounts with few guesses to dodge lockouts. Block the source, alert on distributed attempts, and enforce MFA for all remote access.

alerts.title: Sensitive path probing (content returned)
alerts.summary: 8 request(s) for sensitive paths from 198.51.100.7; 1 returned content
alerts.recommendation: Remove the files from the web root, deny dotfiles at the server, and rotate any credential the exposed file contained.

alerts.title: Injection payloads in requests
alerts.summary: 3 request(s) from 203.0.113.9 contained injection-shaped input (<script, etc/passwd, union select)
alerts.recommendation: Confirm the parameter is handled with prepared statements or output encoding. A 500 or a 200 with unusual content is worth reproducing by hand.

alerts.title: Login endpoint brute force
alerts.summary: 9 failed logins to /login from 192.0.2.77 within 5 minutes
alerts.recommendation: Rate-limit and lock out per account and per source, add a CAPTCHA after a few failures, and require MFA on accounts with access.

alerts.title: Account used from multiple addresses
alerts.summary: 'jsmith' logged in from 2 different addresses within 10 minutes
evidence: Mar 14 03:20:00 web01 sshd[2470]: Accepted publickey for jsmith from 192.0.2.55 port 40200 ssh2
Mar 14 03:21:30 web01 sshd[2472]: Accepted publickey for jsmith from 203.0.113.140 port 40204 ssh2
alerts.recommendation: Confirm with the account owner - a VPN, a jump host, or a scripted job explains some of these. If not, treat it as credential sharing or theft.

alerts.title: Directory and file scanning
alerts.recommendation: Rate-limit the source, front the site with a WAF, and make sure error pages do not confirm which paths exist.
